messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT detected 3812345678 — continuous-batcher latency spike in us-west-2. metric: batch_queue_depth rising, prefetch KVCACHE growth, observed container restarts. Severity: P1. Auto-alerting SRE.
ops-bot: auto-scaling triggered +2 nodes for pool=batchers-usw2 at 13:04:21Z. Prefetch warmup continuing.

maya: i'm seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on batch-03 (gpu0). logs ->
```
[13:03:56] runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[13:04:01] containerd: task exited with status 137
[13:04:02] kubelet: Back-off restarting failed container
```

aj: noticed queue length jump ~x30 after a burst from customer acme-corp. Looks like continuous-batcher acc is growing, not flushing.

sam: acme-corp route shows ~40% 503s across requests in last 3m. dashboard: https://console.redwood/obs/tenant/acme-corp/requests?range=5m

maya: temp mitigation: scaling down batch size + enabling per-tenant hard timeouts. applying config now:
```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  target_batch_size: 8
  max_inflight_per_model: 12
  kv_prefetch: disabled
  soft_timeout_ms: 2000
```

aj: starting rolling drain of pod batch-03 on node g4dn-12xlarge-03 to free GPU mem, moving traffic to fallback variant (gpt-small-quant). command: `kubectl cordon node/g4dn-12xlarge-03 && kubectl drain node/g4dn-12xlarge-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ops-bot: routing update applied: traffic_split(acme-corp) -> {gpt-base: 70%, gpt-small-quant: 30%} for 15m.

leah: i'm coming on-call in 5m. @maya can you summarize what remains after the drain?

maya: after drain, container restarts stopped on batch-03 but batch-02 shows growth. We think a prefetch loop + accumulation bug when node flaps triggers double-enqueue. Repro on staging with long prompt sequences.

sam: customer comms: support pinged acme-corp & created incident INC-2025-684. They reported UI timeouts, no data loss. ETA next update in 30m.

aj: running a live patch: throttle loop to cap accumulator length and add a fast-path eviction if kv_cache_size > 1.2GB. patch: `git rev 8a7f2c9` -> deploying to canary pool now.

maya: note — if we see sigkill (137) recurring after this, fallback to model variant + scale up dedicated capacity for affected tenants.

oncall-bot: @leah assigned as next on-call. Handoff summary: P1 batcher growth causing CUDA OOMs + paging; mitigations applied: drained batch-03, reduced batch size, disabled kv_prefetch, traffic split to fallback. Active work: patch rollout to canary, monitor for 10m, rollback if latency > 2x.

leah: thanks. i'll watch canary and take over. immediate next steps: 1) confirm canary logs for eviction firing, 2) watch OOM events across pool, 3) check paging metrics (swap usage) on hosts. if OOMs persist escalate to infra and consider node replacement.

maya: logs show eviction fired on canary: `kvcache_evict: freed 340MB, accumulator_len drop from 4200->900` — preliminary look good.

sam: customer update posted: "we're mitigating a latency issue affecting some requests; workaround applied and we're rolling a fix. We expect resolution in 1-2 hours." ✅

leah: switching channel to incident bridge, leaving Slack for async notes. transferring thread to incidents if further customer-impact escalation needed. handing off fully to @leah.

oncall-bot: THREAD CLOSED (handoff) — next update expected by 13:35Z unless triggers re-open the incident.
